text:
Amy Chen: FYI Finance wants a repeatable way to forecast spot savings and a chargeback example that shows volatility impact. Can we sketch this quickly? cc @Devon @Sara Kline :eyes:
Devon Patel: I can run a short calc. main knobs: spot price, historical interruption rate by region, fallback fraction (how fast we can fall back to on-demand/dedicated), and preemption penalty (restarts/time lost).
Sara Kline: also want the conservative & 90th pct scenarios for chargeback. ops needs recommended buffer to guarantee SLO.
María López: quick note — regional interruption variance is big. ap-northeast-1 had 2% interruptions last quarter, us-east1 had 7%. that changes expected savings a lot.
Devon Patel: example metric I usually use: effective_unit_cost = spot_price * (1 - interruption_rate) + on_demand_price * fallback_fraction * interruption_rate + preemption_cost_per_unit. using numbers: spot=0.20, on_demand=1.20, interruption_rate=0.07, fallback_fraction=0.6, preemption_cost=0.02
Devon Patel: calc in one line:
```
effective = 0.20*(1-0.07) + 1.20*(0.07*0.6) + 0.02 = 0.186 + 0.0504 + 0.02 = 0.2564 $/GPU-hour
```
Devon Patel: compare to pure on-demand = 1.20 => ~79% savings in this config, but variance matters.
Amy Chen: that helps. how do we present variance? finance wants an expected savings and a 95% worst-case bound for monthly chargeback.
Lee Park: we can bootstrap historical interruption samples per region and simulate month-long workloads with our current autoscaler reaction times. I can spike a run today.
Sara Kline: please include tail risk where multiple zones see interruptions simultaneously. that's what bumped costs last April.
María López: +1. Also include networking egress impact when we move workloads cross-region during fallback — can add 0.01-0.03 $/GPU-hour depending on data plane.
Devon Patel: proposed deliverables: 1) spreadsheet with param inputs + formulas, 2) Monte Carlo sim (30k samples) showing mean/median/95th percentile effective_unit_cost by region, 3) chargeback rates per team with a conservative SLO buffer.
Amy Chen: timeline? Finance wants a short deck by EOD Friday. can we get a preliminary table by tomorrow morning?
Lee Park: I'll run a lightweight sim tonight for us-east1/us-west2 and push results to the sheet.
Devon Patel: I'll draft the formulas and a sample per-team chargeback example (showing how to convert $/GPU-hour to $/inference).
Sara Kline: ops asks that the chargeback includes an explicit "savings credit" line vs on-demand and a separate "variance reserve" line that is allocated monthly.
María López: for mixed pools, we should show two flavors: (A) spot-first with 20% on-demand buffer, (B) balanced 50/50 pinned capacity. different teams may prefer different tradeoffs.
Amy Chen: sounds good. @ops-bot can you snapshot cluster spot utilization last 30 days and upload to the thread? :robot_face:
ops-bot: snapshot uploaded: /data/ops/spot-util/2026-05-11-30d-summary.csv (status: success)
Devon Patel: perfect. I'll pull the historical interruption time series from that file and run regional sims.
Lee Park: action items: I run sim (due: tonight), Devon prepare chargeback examples (due: tomorrow 9am), Sara compile deck (due: Friday EOD). I'll drop results in the sheet and ping here.
Amy Chen: thanks team. keep messages short in the doc; finance will prefer the summary table. :thumbsup:
Sara Kline: one more ask — include unit economics both per-GPU-hour and per-1000-token-equivalent so product teams can relate it to usage.
Devon Patel: noted. I'll create token-equivalent conversion using our average throughput numbers.
Amy Chen: closing note — if the 95th pct pushes cost above committed dedicated price, propose an auto-fallback policy that temporarily pins dedicated nodes for the impacted teams. Mention in deck.
María López: makes sense. tagging risk: cross-region fallback could increase latency; note that as a non-monetary cost.
Lee Park: uploaded preliminary sim csv: /sheets/eng-infra/spot-variance-sim-176501xxx.csv
Amy Chen: great. we'll iterate.
